Detailed Description

----
default implementation of the [[RWCore:RWCore:API:rw::core::debug::IAssertHandler|IAssertHandler]] interface.

Send the assert output to the system channel and break to the debugger if the assert is fatal. If the assert is non-fatal, this function returns false.

This version takes a printf() format and a va_list.

struct rw::shared_globals::internal::AutoOSGlobalPtr::Node

Detailed Description

----
 [[#topofthepage|AutoOSGlobalPtr]] 

Holds a reference to an OS global of the specified type and Id. If the OS global does not exist, a new one is created in the shared heap. The Id parameter is an arbitrary guid and allows the user to have multiple OSGlobalPtrs of the same stored type T.

AutoStaticOSGlobalPtrs and AutoOSGlobalPtrs should not be mixed when referring to a OS global. You should reference an OSGlobal via either one or more AutoOSGlobalPtrs, one or more AutoStaticOSGlobalPtrs, but not both at the same time.

OS global lookup is not very fast so the preferred usage of this class is to wrap it in an accessor. This also ensures that the OS global stays around while created.

This class can safely be used from multiple threads.

Example usage: AutoOSGlobalPtr gpWidget1A; AutoOSGlobalPtr gpWidget1B; AutoOSGlobalPtr gpWidget2;

void Foo() { assert(gpWidget1A == gpWidget1B); assert(gpWidget1A != gpWidget2);

gpWidget1A->DoSomething(); gpWidget2->DoSomething(); }

Example of how to write an accessor wrapper: Foo *GetFoo() { static AutoOSGlobalPtr sPtr; return sPtr; }

Better yet, double-wrap it so clients don't have to include this header:

Foo *InlineGetFoo() { extern void GetFoo(); static Foo * const sPtr = GetFoo(); return sPtr; }

Add two [[RWCore:RWCore:API:rw::BaseResourceDescriptors|BaseResourceDescriptors]] .

The added [[#topofthepage|BaseResourceDescriptor]] must have an alignment less than or equal to the lhs alignment. The resulting [[#topofthepage|BaseResourceDescriptor]] has a size equal to the sum of the lhs size rounded up to a multiple of the alignment of rhs and the size of rhs. Detailed Description

----
A [[#topofthepage|BaseResourceDescriptorType]] is a templated class to allow unique types to be used for specifying [[RWCore:RWCore:API:rw::BaseResourceDescriptors|BaseResourceDescriptors]] for different base resource types. It is important that objects of type [[#topofthepage|BaseResourceDescriptorType]] have the same size as [[RWCore:RWCore:API:rw::BaseResourceDescriptor|BaseResourceDescriptor]] so that we can freely reinterpret cast between the two without slicing. For this reason [[#topofthepage|BaseResourceDescriptorType]] may not add any new members or virtual functions to [[RWCore:RWCore:API:rw::BaseResourceDescriptor|BaseResourceDescriptor]] .

Detailed Description

----
debug [[#topofthepage|Channel]] class.

This class contains the debug [[#topofthepage|Channel]] definition. each debug message is sent to a channel, each channel has one more more devices where the information gets sent to. The constructor takes a pointer to a device as one of it's parameters, this is the default device for this channel. Additional devices can be added and removed using the '' [[#classrw_1_1core_1_1debug_1_1_channel_1737e4685adff3e74294bf065988ac918|AddDevice()]] '' and '' [[#classrw_1_1core_1_1debug_1_1_channel_1b9b75b7ed1abbfe418f75216c48bb97f|RemoveDevice()]] '' member functions.

Please note: instances of this class are NOT THREADSAFE by default. If you need a thread-safe channel, pass rw::core::debug::Channel::FLAG_THREADSAFE to the constructor when the object is created.

Detailed Description

----
Debug device abstract class.

This abstract class provides an interface for sending output to user-defined devices. Since this is an abstract class, in order to use it, a class must be derived from this class and the Output method implemented. Derived classes can be implemented to capture output to files, debuggers, memory buffers, communication devices, etc. Two implementations of devices are included with the RwCore library: [[RWCore:RWCore:API:rw::core::debug::FileDevice|FileDevice]] and [[RWCore:RWCore:API:rw::core::debug::ConsoleDevice|ConsoleDevice]] .

Please note: instances of this class are NOT THREADSAFE by default. If you need a thread-safe device, pass rw::core::debug::Debug::FLAG_THREADSAFE to the constructor when the object is created.

void rw::core::debug::Device::SetBufLen(size_t bufLen)[static]

Set the length of the message buffer (not the data buffer) for all devices created after this one.

Existing devices will be unaffected, only devices created after calling this function will use the new message buffer size. Note that the message buffer is NOT the same as the output buffer. When the devices' print method is called, the maximum length of the output string is limited to the message buffer length.

----
Renderware exception handling class.

You may throw exceptions based directly on this class, or inherit from it to provide your own exception handling functionality.

In addition to the standard what() API, a where() method is provided which specifies the location at which the exception was thrown.

struct [[RWCore:RWCore:API:rw::Factory::SharedData|rw::Factory::SharedData]]

Detailed Description

----
A Generic factory

Generic [[#topofthepage|Factory]] for creating objects of type PRODUCT_T based on a type identifier CLASSID_T. The PRODUCT's creation method is passed a parameter of type PARAM_T when it is invoked.

     It is the caller's responsibility to delete any creator objects which are registered with the factory.

'''See also:'''
      [[#classrw_1_1_factory_120261150fd67bbc6b11e527409fa655d|Factory::ClearRegistry]] only clear's the registries record of registrations, and does not delete the registered creators.
'''Example_usage:'''
    
A factory for creating objects of types inherited from Base, by name. The objects are created with an int parameter. Note that the following code does ''not'' delete the registered creators and therefore leaks memory!



typedef Factory  [[#classrw_1_1_factory_12b05f1206ad1d5f081c28275429a9ec6|Factory]] ;

class Inherted1Creator : public Factory:: [[#classrw_1_1_factory_1aa3bb8d677f1672882f3817cdfcbae55|creator_type]] 
{
    Base *CreateObject(int value)
    {
        return new Inherited1(value);
    }
}

class Inherted2Creator : public Factory:: [[#classrw_1_1_factory_1aa3bb8d677f1672882f3817cdfcbae55|creator_type]] 
{
    Base *CreateObject(int value)
    {
        return new Inherited2(value);
    }
}

void RegisterMoreTypes()
{
    Factory factory; // monostate can be instanced each time it is needed.

    factory.RegisterCreator("inherted2", new Inherited2Creator);
}

int main()
{
    Factory factory;

    factory.RegisterCreator("inherted1", new Inherited1Creator);

    RegisterMoreTypes();

    Base *obj = factory.Create("inherited1", 1);
    Inherted2 = factory.Create("inherited2", 2);

    factory.ClearRegistry();
}



'''Note:'''
     The class is implemented as a MONOSTATE pattern. Each instance of a particular factory specialisation which you create (either dynamically or on the stack) shares the same registry.

Detailed Description

----
A policy used by [[RWCore:RWCore:API:rw::HashContainer|HashContainer]] to specify the memory where the table will be stored. This policy uses a fixed size buffer which is instantiated statically on construction.

CAPACITY is the desired capacity of the hash table. HashTraitsT is a traits class used to obtain the type of objects stored in the [[RWCore:RWCore:API:rw::HashContainer|HashContainer]] including the DefaultContained value which will be used to instantiate the table. Requirements for HashTraitsT are documented in the class documentation for [[RWCore:RWCore:API:rw::HashContainer|HashContainer]] .

 [[RWCore:RWCore:API:rw::LinkListTag|LinkList]]  blockList
uint32_t flags

Detailed Description

----
Represents a free list. Free lists allow same-sized blocks of memory (entries) to be allocated and deallocated at a higher speed than usual. When used with a specific number of entries, the allocation/deallocation speed is suitable for use in high-speed loops.

  • link Used to link all the free lists into a list of free lists.
  • nonAlignedEntrySize Size of a single entry.
  • entrySize Size of a single entry, rounded up to match alignment.
  • entriesPerBlock The number of entries in one block.
  • maxBlocks The maximum number of blocks that can be allocated. Set to 0 for 'no maximum'.
  • alignment The alignment of each entry in the block.
  • hint Not currently used.
  • heapSize The size in bytes of the bitmap of free entries.
  • blockList Holds a double linked list with each block appended to the linked list elements.

class [[RWCore:RWCore:API:rw::HashContainer::IteratorT|rw::HashContainer::IteratorT]]

Detailed Description

----
A hash table class. This class maps a key against a data element. Elements are stored in a table with the index equal

The hashing function and the type of the elements is provided by the HashTraitsT template parameter. The type of buffer used to store the hash table is provided by the BufferPolicy template parameter.

BufferPolicy is used to control where the memory for the [[#topofthepage|HashContainer]] is allocated. Buffer Policy must define: RwSizeT [[#classrw_1_1_hash_container_1e699932fdd7da7bf04e631b86e4016e8|Capacity()]] ; // get the maximum number of elements the container may old RwSizeT GetInitialSize(); // get the initial number of elements in the container

HashTraitsT must define the following: typedef KeyType; // must be copyable typedef DatumType; // must be copyable typedef Contained; // the type of element stored in the hash table, must be copyable static const KeyType BadKey(); returns an invalid keytype to mark nonexistant hashes static const Contained DefaultContained(); returns a default contained object with a key equal to the bad key require EqualTo(GetKey(DefaultContained()), BadKey()) == true static KeyType& GetKey(Contained& obj) static const KeyType& GetKey(const Contained& obj) returns the key element of an object static DatumType& GetData(Contained& obj) static const DatumType& GetData(const Contained& obj) returns the data element of an object static size_t Hash(size_t size, const KeyType &key) Hashing function to use static bool EqualTo(const KeyType& lhs, const KeyType& rhs) Equality test static size_t [[#classrw_1_1_hash_container_1e909e135a6a0449b032291d0c87498e9|GetAlign()]] // Return max alignment of KeyType

Detailed Description

----
Debug Assert Handler interface.

This interface is used to handle asserts after they have failed. This allows the client to implement their own assert handlers if they wish. The RenderWare Core provides an implementation that outputs the assert message to the Debug system channel and aborts.

     ''condition'' the condition that failed, causing the assert.
     ''file'' the source file name the assert originated from.
     ''function'' the name of the function the assert originated from.
     ''line'' the line number the assert originated from.
     ''format'' a message that can provide more information about why the assert failed, this can containprintf()-styleformatting.
     ''argList'' a variable argument list containing the parameters refered to in theformatparameter.
     ''flags'' 0 or one of the AssertFlag bits.

struct rw::LinearResourceAllocator::RestorePoint

Detailed Description

----
A Linear memory allocator. Memory blocks are allocated sequentially on an internal heap until the heap is exhausted. Memory release is handled by getting and setting restore points. All memory allocated after getting a restore point can be deallocated by clearing to that restore point. Freeing individual blocks is a no-op.

void * data

Detailed Description

----
Represents a link on a doubly-linked list. It has a void 'data' pointer which can point to user data. Links are joined in a circular list, with the linked list structure itself holding the 'terminator' element.

  • next Points to the next link in the chain. May point to the current link if there are no elements but the terminator in the linked list.
  • prev Points to the previous link in the chain. May point to the current link if there are no elements but the terminator in the linked list.
  • data Points to user data. This is not initialized in the linked list module, so must be initialized by client if it is to be used.

'''See also:'''

Detailed Description

----
Debug [[#topofthepage|Manager]] .

This is the main Debug [[#topofthepage|Manager]] class. It is a singleton that should get created as early as possible during execution as soon as memory management is available. Once this singleton has been created, the use of debug channels and devices is possible. If the singleton has not been created yet, there are still a number of functions available for use. The static AssertFailed and Abort functions will provide low-level debug functionality that do not depend on any other systems (other than the very low level Hal library) and can be called from static constructors before main() gets executed. This means that assert macros can be used anywhere in the code.

The Debug [[#topofthepage|Manager]] is thread safe.

Member Function Documentation

void rw::core::debug::Manager::Abort(const char *message)[static]

System Abort function.

This function can always be called to abort the system after printing a message to the debug system channel. If the debug [[#topofthepage|Manager]] singleton has not been created yet, it will use the Hal to print and abort.


'''Parameters:'''
     ''message'' the message to print before aborting.

'''See also:'''
      [[#classrw_1_1core_1_1debug_1_1_manager_18b10f922c5e89f267b126d91d99fa78d|HaltSystem]] 

bool rw::core::debug::Manager::AssertFailed(const char *condition, const char *file, const char *function, unsigned int line, const char *format, va_list args, unsigned int flags)[static]

Assert handler.

This function gets called when an assert fails. It is usually called by the rwASSERTM macro but can be called directly when necessary. It does not need the actual debug [[#topofthepage|Manager]] singleton instance. This means asserts can be triggered any time, even from static constructors that get called before main() is executed.


'''Parameters:'''
     ''condition'' the condition that triggered the assert.
     ''file'' the source file where the assert was triggered.
     ''function'' the function where the assert was triggered.
     ''line'' the line number where the assert was triggered.
     ''format'' a user supplied message that provides more information about the assert, inprintf()format.
     ''args'' a va_list containing optional parameters for the format.
     ''flags'' 0 or a combination of the AssertFlags bit-flags.

'''Returns:'''
     true: system must abort, false: assert was ignored.

void rw::core::debug::Manager::DisableChannel(const char *name)

Disable a channel by name.

This function will disable a channel given it's name. If the channel does not exist, the name will be stored in a list and when channels are registered, it will check the list of names of channels that have been disabled. If it exists in the list, the channel will be disabled. The idea behind this mechanism is that during init time a config file containing names of channels to be disabled will be read. The user can now specify which channels to disable to reduce debug output clutter.


'''Parameters:'''
     ''name'' name of the channel to disable.

Detailed Description

A policy used by [[RWCore:RWCore:API:rw::HashContainer|HashContainer]] to specify the memory where the table will be stored. This policy uses memory which has been preallocated by the caller and passed into the class on construction. This memory will be initialized to the DefaultContained value specified by the HashTraits type.

HashTraitsT is a traits class used to obtain the type of objects stored in the [[RWCore:RWCore:API:rw::HashContainer|HashContainer]] including the default value. Requirements for HashTraitsT are documented in the class documentation for [[RWCore:RWCore:API:rw::HashContainer|HashContainer]] .

Detailed Description

----
A policy used by [[RWCore:RWCore:API:rw::HashContainer|HashContainer]] to specify the memory where the table will be stored. This policy uses memory which has been preallocated and preinitialized and passed into the class on construction. This policy class may be used to instantiate a table from a pre-existing table in raw memory.

HashTraitsT is a traits class used to obtain the type of objects stored in the [[RWCore:RWCore:API:rw::HashContainer|HashContainer]] including the default value. Requirements for HashTraitsT are documented in the class documentation for [[RWCore:RWCore:API:rw::HashContainer|HashContainer]] .

Detailed Description

----
Print options for debug messages, used by the [[RWCore:RWCore:API:rw::core::debug::IFormatter|IFormatter]] interface to determine what kind of extra information to include in debug messages.

  • mDate append date to output
  • mTime append time to output
  • mFile append file name to output
  • mLine append line number to output
  • mName append channel name to output
  • mNewLine append a newline character to the output

Detailed Description

----
Class for storing a string, and a hash of that string, which allows for fast string comparisons. Because the hash is not unique, comparison between two instances with a matching hash results in a normal string comparison. Comparison between two instances with non-matching hashes is however much faster, being the result of a single integer comparison.

Relative to the time taken to compare two identical strings, tests indicate that it takes approximately 1.33 times longer to calculate the hash for one of the strings. Comparison between strings with the same hash incurs the extra hash comparison. Comparison between strings with a different hash is a constant time operation.

Detailed Description

----
Implements a shared pointer object.

ValueType has no restrictions.

  • m_ptr Please treat this as private. It is public only because member template friends are not supported by all compilers (eg gcc <= 2.97 and MSVC <= 7.1).
  • m_count Please treat this as private. It is public only because member template friends are not supported by all compilers (eg gcc <= 2.97 and MSVC <= 7.1).

Detailed Description

----
 [[#topofthepage|RwStringStream]] allows formatted input and output via a C++ IOStream like mechanism using << and >> operators to insert and extract data from an RwString stream representation. It is intended to behave like a C++ std::stringstream.

  • mStream The stream .
  • mpPos The position in the stream where the next put will happen.
  • mgPos The position in the stream where the next get will happen.
  • mWidth The output width of the stream.
  • mPrec The output precision of stream.
  • mFmtFlags The IO Stream format flags.
  • mStateFlags The flags for the current state of the stream.

In a subsequent ballot round:

Landon Curt Noll ( [http://www.isthe.com/chongo/ http://www.isthe.com/chongo/] )

improved on their algorithm. Some people tried this hash and found that it worked rather well. In an EMail message to Landon, they named it the ``Fowler/Noll/Vo'' or FNV hash.

FNV hashes are designed to be fast while maintaining a hashValue. collision rate. The FNV speed alhashValue.s one to quickly hash lots of data while maintaining a reasonable collision rate. See:

[http://www.isthe.com/chongo/tech/comp/fnv/index.html http://www.isthe.com/chongo/tech/comp/fnv/index.html]

for more details as well as other forms of the FNV hash.

Detailed Description

----
Contains core macros, types, templates and classes that are used in both conditioning and runtime code. There are many undocumented types in this namespace; these are generally only used by packages that are derived from the former RenderWare Platform SDK.

 [[RWCore:RWCore:API:rw::LinkListTag|LinkList]]  rw::rw_FreeListList

This is a doubly-linked list that holds references to all the free lists currently in use by the client. It is not used unless rw_TRACKFREELISTS is defined. If it is used then all remaining linked list links will be automatically released when the free list module is shut down, as will the linked list structures themselves.

void * rw::FreeListAlloc( [[RWCore:RWCore:API:rw::FreeList|FreeList]] *freeList, uint32_t hint)

Retrieves an unused entry from the specified free list. If, prior to this function call, the free list is empty, the whole free list block is allocated memory. If there are no more unused entries left, a new block is allocated, and an entry is returned from it.

In debug mode, the entry's memory will be initialized with the value defined in rw_ALLOCINITVAL.


'''Parameters:'''
     ''freelist'' Pointer to the free list.
     ''hint'' Not currently used. Set to 0.

'''Returns:'''
     A pointer to an unused entry if successful or 0 if there is an error.

'''See also:'''
      [[#namespacerw_10e6f7dc942688da1d7edd0c6ceaeb403|FreeListInitialize]]  [[#namespacerw_140ed0b11d3341af1899fadee145e54c8|FreeListPurge]]  [[#namespacerw_1cea41ee312376dacd674d0549e1cef0e|FreeListForAllUsed]]  [[#namespacerw_181565a8506b6df3b8ee321359fa54c03|FreeListRelease]]  [[#namespacerw_15600372c7158997ee74a468382cb6a77|FreeListPurgeAllFreeLists]] 

 [[RWCore:RWCore:API:rw::FreeList|FreeList]] * rw::FreeListForAllUsed( [[RWCore:RWCore:API:rw::FreeList|FreeList]] *freeList,  [[#namespacerw_18e57b94585dbab0ca1a93d775ff70667|FreeListCallBack]]  fpCallBack, void *pData)

Applies the given callback function to all used entries in the specified free list. The format of the callback function is:

     void (* [[#namespacerw_18e57b94585dbab0ca1a93d775ff70667|FreeListCallBack]] )(void *mem, void *data);
where "data" is a pointer to user-defined data pointer to pass to the callback function.


'''Parameters:'''
     ''freeList'' A pointer to the free list.
     ''fpCallBack'' A pointer to the callback to call for each used block.
     ''pData'' A pointer to user-supplied data to pass to the callback function.

'''Returns:'''
     A pointer to the free list if successful or 0 if there is an error.

'''See also:'''
      [[#namespacerw_10760cd07bb639d6cfa43e44a42982f82|FreeListAlloc]]  [[#namespacerw_10e6f7dc942688da1d7edd0c6ceaeb403|FreeListInitialize]]  [[#namespacerw_13c6d9f9f0962fcb9aaf8adfe14382dc0|FreeListFree]]  [[#namespacerw_140ed0b11d3341af1899fadee145e54c8|FreeListPurge]]  [[#namespacerw_181565a8506b6df3b8ee321359fa54c03|FreeListRelease]]  [[#namespacerw_15600372c7158997ee74a468382cb6a77|FreeListPurgeAllFreeLists]]

'''Parameters:'''

     ''entry'' The entry to be freed.

'''Returns:'''

uint32_t rw::FreeListGetSize(uint32_t entrySize, uint32_t entriesPerBlock, uint32_t alignment, uint32_t blocks, uint32_t maxBlocks)

 [[RWCore:RWCore:API:rw::FreeList|FreeList]] * rw::FreeListInitialize(void *ptr, uint32_t entrySize, uint32_t entriesPerBlock, uint32_t alignment, uint32_t blocks, uint32_t maxBlocks, uint32_t hint)

Creates an empty free list, using the memory given to it if a non-zero pointer is passed in. Some blocks may be preallocated to attempt to prevent a delay from occurring during the later execution of client code when a new entry is requested.

The initialized free list must be released later by FreeListRelease.


'''Parameters:'''
     ''entrySize'' The size in bytes of a single entry.
     ''entriesPerBlock'' The number of entries is a single block. This must be a multiple of 8.
     ''alignment'' The alignment which entries will have. This must be given to prevent a warning from appearing in debug mode.
     ''blocks'' The number of blocks to preallocate.
     ''freeList'' Pointer to preallocated memory for new free list. If this is 0, memory will be allocated in this module.
     ''hint'' Not currently used. Set to 0.

'''Returns:'''
     A pointer to the newly-created free list, or 0 on failure.

'''See also:'''
      [[#namespacerw_181565a8506b6df3b8ee321359fa54c03|FreeListRelease]]

Semi private method for calling the registered RwDebugMessageCallback, used by the debug macros to access the global debug hooks. Users wanting to write their own macros can use this interface to call the global debug hooks.

Get n=1..4 bytes of a big endian uint32_t from memory.

TO [[#lexicalcast_8h_19ea73512cb3dae19a4bc2361b8b136fd|RwLexicalCast]](FROM f)

Detailed Description

----
Simple boost::lexical_cast workalike for converting between string and numeric values.

Function Documentation

----
template
template
TO RwLexicalCast(FROM f)[inline]

Casts a FROM into a TO

Casts a FROM into a TO using an [[RWCore:RWCore:API:RwStringStream|RwStringStream]] .
     Use it to convert a numerical value into a string, or vice versa:

    int32_t  value = 1234;
    RwString intAsString = RwLexicalCast(value);

    RwString realAsString = "3.1415";
    float32_t realvalue = RwLexicalCast(realvalue);

'''Note:'''
     All 8 bit types are treated as characters. If you want to convert an int8 into a string, you have to cast it into an int16 or int32 first.

    int8_t i = 65;
    RwString intAsString0 = RwLexicalCast(i);          // gives "A"
    RwString intAsString1 = RwLexicalCast((int32_t)i); // gives "65"

Define Documentation

----
#define RWFREELISTFLAG_FREEBLOCKS 1

This flag, which can be set/cleared through a call to FreeListSetFlags, causes blocks that have no used entries to be freed immediately. New freelists have this flag set by default.


'''See also:'''
     FreeList [[RWCore:RWCore:API:rw#namespacerw_1b48fe935b4644f58ffd56fc1bd026370|FreeListGetFlags]]  [[RWCore:RWCore:API:rw#namespacerw_1a83784d3744b197dc97ace1c058ec509|FreeListSetFlags]] 

#define RWFREELISTFLAG_STATIC 2

This flag is set for a free list internally. If memory is passed into the free list module to make a new free list from, this flag is set. This is to ensure that the free list module does not release this memory when FreeListRelease is called.


'''See also:'''
     FreeList [[RWCore:RWCore:API:rw#namespacerw_1b48fe935b4644f58ffd56fc1bd026370|FreeListGetFlags]]

#define RWMEMORYFUNCTIONS_NEWANDDELETE void *operator new(size_t size) \ { \ rwFUNCTION(); \ rwRETURN(RwMalloc(size)); \ } \ void operator delete(void *memory) \ { \ rwFUNCTION(); \ RwFree(memory); \ rwRETURNVOID(); \ } \ void *operator new(size_t RWUNUSED(size), void *memory) \ { \ rwFUNCTION(); \ rwRETURN(memory); \ } \ void operator delete(void *, void *) \ { \ rwFUNCTION(); \ rwRETURNVOID(); \ }

Per-class overrides of new and delete, including standard and placement versions of each. These are simple wrappers for RwMalloc and RwFree. The placement delete is required only to satisfy constructors which may throw exceptions.

RwChar * rwGenericSprintf(const RwChar *format, ... )

rwGenericSprintf inline version of printf style argument list to string.
'''Parameters:'''
     ''format'' The 'printf' style format string / text.
     ''...'' The variable argument list for the parameters of the printf string.

'''Returns:'''
     A string holding the formatted text. Do NOT delete this string. The maximum length of this string is dictated by the rw_MAXGENERICSPRINTFSTRINGLEN value.

RwChar * rwGenericSprintfVL(const RwChar *format, va_list args)

rwGenericSprintfVL takes a va_list and so can be called by a function who's input is a variable argument list (...) such as rwGenericSprintf or rwDebugGenericSprintf.
'''Parameters:'''
     ''format'' The 'printf' style format string / text.
     ''args'' The variable argument list for the parameters of the printf string (already had va_start applied to it).

'''Returns:'''
     A string holding the formatted text. Do NOT delete this string. The maximum length of this string

void * RwMemcpy(void *, const void *, size_t )

RwMemcpy Copies memory from source to destination. Asserts if the buffers overlap. Use RwMemmove to copy data if the buffers may overlap.
'''Parameters:'''
     ''dst'' Memory location to copy data to.
     ''src'' Memory location to copy data from.
     ''nbytes'' Number of bytes to copy

'''Returns:'''
     The value of dst.

'''See also:'''
      [[RWCore:RWCore:API:rwstring.cpp#rwstring_8cpp_1c970f0577cac9385f14866e2d44b56c4|RwMemmove]] 

void * RwMemmove(void *, const void *, size_t )

RwMemmove Copies memory from source to destination. The source and destination buffers may overlap. We use own own implementation because on PS3, memmove can still call memcpy even if the buffer overlap, which is possibly unsafe.
'''Parameters:'''
     ''dst'' Memory location to copy data to.
     ''src'' Memory location to copy data from.
     ''nbytes'' Number of bytes to copy

'''Returns:'''
     The value of dst.

'''See also:'''
     RwMemcopy

int32_t RwSnprintf(RwChar *buffer, size_t count, const RwChar *format, ... )

An _snprintf() wrapper. If this platform does not have a _vsnprintf() function then this function is unsafe.


'''Parameters:'''
     ''buffer'' Target buffer for output.
     ''count'' Maximum number of characters to write. If this platform does not have a _vsnprintf function then this parameter is *ignored*.
     ''format'' Format specification.
     ''argptr'' Pointer to list of arguments.

'''Returns:'''
     The same as _snprintf. Returns the number of characters written to the given buffer, excluding NULL termination.

RwChar * RwStristr(RwChar *string1, const RwChar *string2)

Determine if a string exists within another string, with a case insensitive comparison.


'''Parameters:'''
     ''string1'' The string to be searched
     ''string2'' The string to search for

'''Returns:'''
     Pointer to the string to search for within the source string, or NULL if not found

int32_t RwVsnprintf(char *buffer, size_t count, const RwChar *format, va_list argptr)

An unsafe _vsnprintf() wrapper. The 'count' parameter is ignored and the target string is assumed to have enough space.


'''Parameters:'''
     ''buffer'' Target buffer for output.
     ''count'' *UNUSED* Maximum number of characters to write.
     ''format'' Format specification.
     ''argptr'' Pointer to list of arguments.

'''Returns:'''
     The same as _snprintf. Returns the number of characters written to the given buffer, excluding NULL termination.

#define RW_CORE_CREATE_VERSION_NUMBER ((major_ver) * 1000000 + (minor_ver) * 1000 + (patch_ver))

This is a utility macro that users may use to create a single version number that can be compared against RW_CORE_VERSION.

For example:



 #if RW_CORE_VERSION > RW_CORE_CREATE_VERSION_NUMBER( 1, 1, 0 )
 printf("Core version is greater than 1.1.0.\n");
 #endif
#define RW_CORE_VERSION RW_CORE_CREATE_VERSION_NUMBER( RW_CORE_VERSION_MAJOR, RW_CORE_VERSION_MINOR, RW_CORE_VERSION_PATCH )

This macro is an aggregate of the major, minor and patch version numbers.

In debug mode, allocated blocks are initialized to this value.

#define rw_TRACKFREELISTS 

When this is defined, any free lists that are released by the client are not freed, in case the client later wishes to have a new free list. Instead, they are freed when the module shuts down instead.
#define rw_USEMASTERFORNEWFREELISTSx 

When this is defined, new free lists created with FreeListInitialize are not made with RwMalloc, but are themselves created through this single free list of free list structures.

Function Documentation

----
RwChar * rwGenericSprintf(const RwChar *format, ... )

rwGenericSprintf inline version of printf style argument list to string.
'''Parameters:'''
     ''format'' The 'printf' style format string / text.
     ''...'' The variable argument list for the parameters of the printf string.

'''Returns:'''
     A string holding the formatted text. Do NOT delete this string. The maximum length of this string is dictated by the rw_MAXGENERICSPRINTFSTRINGLEN value.

RwChar * rwGenericSprintfVL(const RwChar *format, va_list args)

rwGenericSprintfVL takes a va_list and so can be called by a function who's input is a variable argument list (...) such as rwGenericSprintf or rwDebugGenericSprintf.
'''Parameters:'''
     ''format'' The 'printf' style format string / text.
     ''args'' The variable argument list for the parameters of the printf string (already had va_start applied to it).

'''Returns:'''
     A string holding the formatted text. Do NOT delete this string. The maximum length of this string

void * RwMemcpy(void *dst, const void *src, size_t nbytes)

RwMemcpy Copies memory from source to destination. Asserts if the buffers overlap. Use RwMemmove to copy data if the buffers may overlap.
'''Parameters:'''
     ''dst'' Memory location to copy data to.
     ''src'' Memory location to copy data from.
     ''nbytes'' Number of bytes to copy

'''Returns:'''
     The value of dst.

'''See also:'''
      [[#rwstring_8cpp_1c970f0577cac9385f14866e2d44b56c4|RwMemmove]] 

void * RwMemmove(void *dst, const void *src, size_t nbytes)

RwMemmove Copies memory from source to destination. The source and destination buffers may overlap. We use own own implementation because on PS3, memmove can still call memcpy even if the buffer overlap, which is possibly unsafe.
'''Parameters:'''
     ''dst'' Memory location to copy data to.
     ''src'' Memory location to copy data from.
     ''nbytes'' Number of bytes to copy

'''Returns:'''
     The value of dst.

'''See also:'''
     RwMemcopy

int32_t RwSnprintf(RwChar *buffer, size_t count, const RwChar *format, ... )

An _snprintf() wrapper. If this platform does not have a _vsnprintf() function then this function is unsafe.


'''Parameters:'''
     ''buffer'' Target buffer for output.
     ''count'' Maximum number of characters to write. If this platform does not have a _vsnprintf function then this parameter is *ignored*.
     ''format'' Format specification.
     ''argptr'' Pointer to list of arguments.

'''Returns:'''
     The same as _snprintf. Returns the number of characters written to the given buffer, excluding NULL termination.

RwChar * RwStristr(RwChar *string1, const RwChar *string2)

Determine if a string exists within another string, with a case insensitive comparison.


'''Parameters:'''
     ''string1'' The string to be searched
     ''string2'' The string to search for

'''Returns:'''
     Pointer to the string to search for within the source string, or NULL if not found

int32_t RwVsnprintf(char *buffer, size_t count, const RwChar *format, va_list args)

An unsafe _vsnprintf() wrapper. The 'count' parameter is ignored and the target string is assumed to have enough space.


'''Parameters:'''
     ''buffer'' Target buffer for output.
     ''count'' *UNUSED* Maximum number of characters to write.
     ''format'' Format specification.
     ''argptr'' Pointer to list of arguments.

'''Returns:'''
     The same as _snprintf. Returns the number of characters written to the given buffer, excluding NULL termination.

----
Simple std::stringstream workalike for formatted input/output to and from an RwString.

const RwChar * SelectBaseFormat( [[RWCore:RWCore:API:RwStringStream|RwStringStream]] &stream, const RwChar *octFmt, const RwChar *decFmt, const RwChar *hexFmt)[static]

Selects one of the supplied format strings (one for oct, dec and hex) to use for reading a number by examining the stream's flags and (if the all basefields are clear) the prefix ("0" or "0x").
'''Library:''' rwstl


'''Parameters:'''
     ''stream'' The stream to read from.
     ''octFmt'' The format string to select if the number is to be read in octal.
     ''decFmt'' The format string to select if the number is to be read in decimal.
     ''hexFmt'' The format string to select if the number is to be read in hexadecimal.

'''Returns:'''
     One of the supplied format strings, as appropriate for the detected base.
